house.why: Cairo's Mamluk star geometry (Sultan Hassan, al-Azhar woodwork, Khan el-Khalili brass) is the city's highest craft and is still printed by state and mosque alike.

ideologies.name: State Nationalism

fit.variant: Dense ranks of filled 8-point stars joined by diagonal bands: ordered, martial and regular, in the red of the tricolour.
fit.emblem: A plain military shield, the guardian state without the eagle.

ideologies.why: Close-set banded stars like a parade ground; tricolour red on dark ground; the shield of the guardian army.

ideologies.name: Nasserism

fit.variant: Bold 8-ray bursts meeting tip to tip at scale 1, echoing Nasser-era sun-ray posters; defiant gold on dark.
fit.emblem: The five-pointed star of the United Arab Republic flag.

ideologies.why: Large confident ray bursts recall star-and-ray posters; mill-worker gold; the UAR star.

ideologies.name: Liberalism

fit.variant: Open intersecting rings with light dots where they meet: airy, hopeful, much open ground, in Mediterranean blue.
fit.emblem: The 1919 crescent embracing the cross of national unity.

ideologies.why: Airy interlocking rings for an open civil state; Alexandrian blue; crescent-and-cross of Muslim-Copt unity.

ideologies.name: Islamism

fit.variant: Layered 12-point rosettes of Mamluk mosque ornament, patient and pious, in Freedom and Justice green.
fit.emblem: The open Quran, the book at the heart of the movement.

ideologies.why: Mamluk 12-point rosettes for a disciplined devout creed; FJP green; the open book.

ideologies.name: Salafism

fit.variant: A sparse line-only interlaced 8-point star net, no fills: austere and rigorous but keeping its knots, teal on near-black.
fit.emblem: The plain crescent, an aniconic mark of faith.

ideologies.why: Bare interlaced star lines for an austere, aniconic creed; deep teal; the crescent.

factions.name: Egyptian Armed Forces high command

factions.name: Society of the Muslim Brothers (Muslim Brotherhood) and its Freedom and Justice Party
factions.why: The crescent in the Freedom and Justice Party's green.

factions.name: Salafist Call (al-Da'wa al-Salafiyya) and its Nour Party
factions.why: Nour means light: a simple flame.

factions.name: Ministry of Interior, the Central Security Forces and State Security Investigations
factions.why: A watchtower for the police and surveillance state.

factions.name: National Democratic Party networks and the Mubarak-era business elite (the feloul, 'remnants')
factions.why: The coin of the tycoons and patronage networks.

factions.name: Revolution Youth Coalition and the April 6 Youth Movement
factions.why: A plain star of hope for the youth who held Tahrir.

patrons.name: United States of America
patrons.why: The star of the Stars and Stripes.
